recommendation_summary: Action now: replace the endpoint's row loading and in-memory counting with one SQL COUNT in the existing application and PostgreSQL. Optional addition: an index on the unpaid condition, only if the query is still slow. No new service or topic this week, and Kafka, CQRS and Redis are rejected. Unmet needs: no latency was measured, and the query and schema were not inspected.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Unpaid-invoice count under one second, matching invoices committed at request time (you). An approved Kafka budget and peers moving to events are not requirements for this count.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, a CQRS projection, Redis, and any new service or topic. A projection lags commit time and adds systems this count does not need.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads invoice rows, builds objects, and counts them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: You said the endpoint returns only that count, has no other reader, and users report it is slow. The query and schema were not inspected.

note: The four record lines come before a bounded SQL COUNT fix that keeps request-time freshness, and the index is only a conditional next step.
